02 The research question

What happens
to the air
above us?

Atmospheric measurements connect abstract scientific ideas with something observable. This project develops a practical platform through which learners could explore sensors, computing and environmental data.

A Raspberry Pi brings environmental and particulate sensing into one programmable instrument. The research follows Design Science Research: build an artefact, evaluate it, and refine it through evidence.

The balloon is the intended research platform. This visual descent is an interpretation of that ambition. The measurements presented here were collected on the ground in the Honours Laboratory.

Small components.
A complete path
from air to data.

The exposed bench-top prototype integrates sensing, Python processing, local visualisation and remote transmission. An Enviro+ board sits above the Raspberry Pi; the PMS5003 connects to its dedicated particulate interface.

SENSE → PROCESS → DISPLAY → RECORD
Laboratory tests used mains power. A flight enclosure and flight-specific power supply remain to be evaluated.

Environmental

BME280

Temperature, relative humidity and barometric pressure.

Particulate

PMS5003

PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 mass concentrations.

Context

MICS6814 + LTR559

Gas-related response, light and proximity sensing.

Interface

ST7735 LCD

Local readings and short histories, with proximity-based navigation.

04 A rhythm of observation

One observationevery 20.033seconds.

The system was configured around a 20-second acquisition and upload cadence. The average interval in the preserved local record was 20.033 seconds, measured between consecutive timestamps.

Unavailable PM readings use −1 and must be counted separately.

The record demonstrates repeated acquisition under laboratory conditions. Stable timing and complete records support a functional assessment of the prototype; they do not establish laboratory-grade measurement accuracy.

Temperature readings may include Raspberry Pi heating. The NH₃ channel is a relative sensor index, not a calibrated ammonia concentration. Flight performance requires its own evidence.

06 Reading the evidence

A working artefact.
An open investigation.

Established on the ground

What we know.

The prototype brings environmental, particulate and gas-related sensing into one Raspberry Pi application, with local display and a record that can be analysed over time.

The selected laboratory window contains 525 observations with consistent acquisition intervals. The preserved measurements support assessment of the system’s preliminary technical operation.

Still to be evaluated

What comes next.

A separate flight evaluation must examine low pressure, changing temperature, payload motion, power constraints and telemetry. Ground results cannot establish stratospheric performance.

The educational motivation also needs its own evaluation. The current technical study does not demonstrate learning gains or classroom usability through direct testing with learners.

DESIGN SCIENCE RESEARCH / BUILD → TEST → REFLECT → REFINE
The artefact and its evidence develop together.
